title: Common prohibited uses across three providers

opening.headline: The usage policy is dozens of pages long, so how can we determine whether our work is permitted or prohibited?
body: When a question arises in the field, “Can this function be made with AI?”, the person in charge opens the model provider’s usage policy. However, the policy is long and is structured differently for each company, so even if you read it from beginning to end, the boundaries are hard to see.

In this class, you will learn how to read the policies of three companies, Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google, side by side in the same framework. Judging is much easier if you read the policy not in document order but by dividing it into categories: Prohibitions, Restrictions, Exceptions, and Enforcement. Finally, we will apply this method to a customer service chatbot case.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: The common prohibited categories of the three companies' usage policies can be explained.
Policy items can be divided into prohibited, restricted, and permitted categories.

screens.title: Is this request allowed or prohibited?
screens.lead:
There are three requests from the field. As you select each request, you'll see hints about which policy item it's hitting. First, decide for yourself whether it is allowed or prohibited, and then click it.

Policy base date: 2026-10-23. Distinguish between the version currently in effect and the version scheduled to be implemented. Anthropic has released the 2026-11-12 enforcement version, so you should check again for changes in the enforcement date and high-risk areas and disclosure obligations before actual operation.

visual.alt: A scene with three business request cards and a question mark on the right.
labels: Quantifying the level of anger in phone calls
AI solely determines credit limit approval

items.prompt: Request 1: I would like to have a chatbot that drafts answers to customer inquiries.
items.answer: This is the most common use. This request itself is not in the ban category as it does not fall on any of the ban lists in the three company policies. However, if the chatbot is talking directly with the customer, you need to check other items separately, such as whether it is pretending to be a human.

items.prompt: Request 2: I would like to add a function to quantify the level of anger in customer phone calls.
items.answer: This corresponds to emotional reasoning. OpenAI blocks inferring an individual's emotions in workplace and educational settings, while Anthropic blocks emotion recognition systems except for medical or safety purposes. Unlike request 1, this touches directly on the policy's restrictions and requires careful review.

items.prompt: Request 3: I would like to have AI solely decide whether to approve a credit limit or not.
items.answer: This corresponds to automatic decision making. Google bans automated decisions in high-risk areas that significantly disadvantage individual rights without human oversight, and OpenAI also prevents high-risk decisions in sensitive areas, including finance, from being automated without human review.

screens.outro: Although all three requests use AI, their policy positions are different. Now let's think about your experience.

screens.title: Have you ever read the policy all the way through?
screens.lead: Select questions one by one to see how the instructor organizes his thoughts. You won't be typing or submitting your answer, so think about it in your head first and then unfold it.

items.prompt: Have you ever read the entire usage policy from cover to cover?
items.answer: Most people only read parts of it or search for it when they need it. It's natural. The goal of this class is not to memorize the full text, but to know in which category to look for the item you need.

items.prompt: Were there any items that you skipped over while reading because they were unrelated to our work?
items.answer: Some of the items I skipped are actually unrelated, but if you break it down into business functions, there are surprisingly many items that are touched upon. For example, even simple customer-facing functions reach the limit when combined with emotional reasoning or automated decisions.

items.prompt: Have you ever thought that the acceptability of doing the same work across two company models would be different?
items.answer: Common prohibited areas remain the same across companies, but the terms and wording of restricted categories vary from company to company. So, you shouldn't just check one company's policy and apply it to other company models as well. The next screen begins with a side-by-side comparison of the three documents.

screens.outro: Regardless of the level of reading experience, we will look at the structure of the policy document from the same perspective.

screens.title: Place the table of contents of three documents side by side
screens.lead: Select each tab to find out how each company's policies are structured. It's a good idea to look at the tabs alternately to find differences and commonalities in the way they are organized.

tabs.label: Anthropic
tabs.body: Anthropic Usage Policy is divided into three branches. **Universal Usage Standards** are prohibitions that apply to all users and all uses. **High-risk Use Case Requirements** are requirements for specific uses that pose an increased risk to individuals. **Additional Use Case Guidelines** cover use cases such as consumer-facing chatbots and agents, products targeting minors, and agentic use. The policy focuses on how products are used and does not ban entire industries.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body: OpenAI Usage policies list prohibitions in four groups: **Protect people** is a safe area for things like threats, self-harm, violence, weapons, illegal activities, and violations of other people's systems. **Respect privacy** is an area related to personal information, such as facial recognition databases, social scoring, and emotional inference. **Keep minors safe** covers protecting under-18s, and **Empower people** covers deception and fraud, as well as automating high-risk decisions in sensitive areas without human review.

tabs.label: Google
tabs.body: The Google Generative AI Prohibited Use Policy consists of four sections, numbered 1 through 4. Number 1 refers to dangerous or illegal activity, number 2 refers to security violations of others or Google services, number 3 refers to sexual, violent or hateful content, and number 4 refers to disinformation and deceptive activities. Under number 1, automated decisions without human supervision in high-risk areas are included as a sub-item.

tabs.label: common ground
tabs.body: Although they are constructed differently, two layers are visible. One is a floor that is prohibited to everyone, and the other is a floor that is restricted under certain conditions. Therefore, when reading the three documents, do not follow the order of the table of contents, but first indicate which layer each item belongs to to make comparison easier.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the structure, let’s extract the prohibited categories that overlap the three documents from the content.

screens.title: All three companies block equally
screens.lead: Below is a list of prohibited categories commonly found in the three documents. When you select a highlighted passage, an explanation appears as to why that category is the bottom line in your company's standards.

data.text: Common Prohibited Categories: Child sexual exploitation content, Promoting violent extremism and terrorism, Weapons Development and Procurement, Sexual images without consent, Self-contradictory claims, Scams, spam, phishing, and malware, Impersonation, Use of personal information and biometric information without consent, Bypass safety device

marks.note: OpenAI's CSAM ban, Google's child sexual abuse and exploitation ban, and Anthropic's Universal Usage Standards are all covered. This is the clearest prohibition to which it is difficult to make exceptions.
Google bans promoting violent extremism and terrorism, while OpenAI bans terrorism and violence. This is confirmed in all three documents.
OpenAI prevents the development, procurement, and use of weapons, including conventional weapons and CBRNEs. Two other companies also have weapons-related bans.
Google banned the promotion of sexual images without consent, and OpenAI banned sexual violence and intimate content without consent.
Google Section 2 covers spam, phishing, and malware, and Section 4 covers fraud and deception. OpenAI stops fraud, spam, and malicious cyber activity.

marks.span: Use of personal information and biometric information without consent
marks.note: Google prohibits the use of personal or biometric information without consent as required by law. OpenAI bans facial recognition databases without consent.
Google prohibits manipulating models to bypass abuse prevention devices or safety filters, and OpenAI prohibits circumvention of safeguards.

screens.outro: Common prohibitions are areas that are unlikely to be tolerated even if you change companies, so they serve as the bottom line of your company's standards. Next, let's look at the areas where conditions are attached.

screens.title: How are prohibitions and restrictions read differently?
screens.lead: Tap the toggle to alternate between when the same task, the automatic decision, is read as Prohibited and when it is read as Restricted. The differences between the two categories are explained, as well as exceptions and enforcement methods.

states.label: Prohibited Category
states.body: Prohibition is an area where something is not permitted even if conditions are met. This includes the list of common prohibitions seen earlier. The function of this area is not to modify the design, but rather not to do it. Enforcement goes up step by step. The Gemini API documentation outlines the following sequential steps: email contact, temporary usage restrictions, suspension, and account closure, noting that closure is a last resort for serious violations. To monitor for abuse, the Gemini API retains prompts, additional context, and output for 55 days. The document explains that the stored data is used only for policy enforcement purposes and is not used to learn models other than those for policy enforcement. When we notify you of a suspension or closure, we will also provide a link to appeal. As such, enforcement comes with warnings and appeal procedures.

states.label: restricted category
states.body: Restrictions are not prohibitions, but rather areas with conditions attached. Google prevents automated decisions in high-risk areas that place individuals at a significant disadvantage without human oversight. OpenAI prevents the provision of personalized, licensed legal and medical advice without the involvement of relevant professionals and the complete automation of high-stakes decisions in sensitive areas. In other words, having human review opens the door. There are also exceptions. Note that exceptions are a separate layer that loosens restrictions. Anthropic writes that with the exception of security research with permission from the system owner, Google may make exceptions for educational, archival, scientific or artistic considerations.

screens.outro: Now that you have learned the criteria for classifying categories, let's apply them to real-life examples.

screens.title: Commentary: Where do customer service chatbots reach?
screens.lead: The instructor will break down the shopping mall customer service chatbot into four steps. This chatbot performs order inquiries, refund information, product recommendations, and classification of dissatisfied customers. Select the next arrow to skip a step.

steps.title: Step 1: Break down the function
steps.body: Instead of judging the entire chatbot as a lump, divide it by function. Order tracking, refund notifications, product recommendations, and drafting responses are common uses and are therefore not subject to the ban for all three companies. One area that can be problematic is features that evaluate people, such as customer categorization, so we look at these features in more detail in the next step.

steps.title: Step 2: Look at the data being handled
steps.body: If classifying a dissatisfied customer is a method of inferring the customer's emotions from phone calls or chat sentences and converting them into numbers, it reaches emotional inference. OpenAI limits emotional inference to workplace and educational environments, while Anthropic limits emotion recognition systems to non-medical or safety purposes. When analyzing agent calls, the workplace environment must also be taken into consideration.

steps.title: Step 3: See the decisions the AI makes
steps.body: If the AI alone confirms the refund refusal, it becomes an automatic decision without human supervision. Since this is a decision that could result in a financial penalty for the customer, it can reach Google's Automated Decision section and OpenAI's High-Risk Decision Automation section. The key to this step is who makes the final decision.

steps.title: Step 4: See if you are pretending to be human
steps.body: If a chatbot is set up to respond as if it were a human agent, it creates a deception that makes you believe you are talking to a human. Anthropic prevents people from tricking you into thinking you're interacting with a human, and we also stop Google from fooling you into thinking it's human-made. The simplest solution is to announce that you are a chatbot.

steps.title: Organize with scorecard
steps.body: If organized by function, order inquiry, refund information, product recommendation, and answer draft are irrelevant. Emotion quantification falls into the restricted category, and single confirmation of refund refusal also falls into the restricted category. Setting up a response that pretends to be a human touches the prohibition against deception. It is important that even for a single chatbot, each function has a different location.

screens.outro: Now that the reaching function has been confirmed, let's see how to fix it to suit the conditions.

screens.title: Explanation: How to fix reach function
screens.lead: Click the toggle to compare how the same chatbot flow differs between the original design and the revised design. The instructor points out which policy statement each change is based on.

states.label: original design
states.body: AI scores the degree of anger from the sentences sent by the customer and the voice of the call, and if the number is high, it classifies the customer as a dissatisfied customer. For refund requests, AI immediately confirms approval or rejection according to the rules and notifies the customer. The first screen displays the agent's name and profile photo, making it easy to misunderstand that you are talking to a human. This design hits three things at once: emotional reasoning, automatic decisions without human supervision, and deception.

states.label: revised design
states.body: Emotion quantification is excluded and the inquiry is categorized by the type of inquiry chosen by the customer. Unfavorable decisions, such as refusal of refunds, are drafted by AI and finalized by the person in charge, with human review included. On the first screen, it is announced that it is an AI chatbot and a path is provided to transfer to human consultation. Lastly, record the supporting document and location of which document and which phrase the change was made based on. This is what reading policies by categories actually looks like. Even with the revised design, features such as drafting answers and order tracking remain the same, so the core value of the chatbot is not diminished and only the items it touches are organized according to the conditions. When modifying a design, first check what the original purpose was, and then choose the appropriate method for each item: whether to remove a feature, add a human review, or add a notice.

screens.outro: Now that I have finished explaining the case, I will summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key Takeaway: Read policies by category
screens.lead: We organize what we have seen so far into one reading method. Read the paragraph below and think about how it applies to your work.

paragraphs: The usage policy is not a document that you read from start to finish, but rather a document that you browse and read by dividing it into categories. First, break down your business functions into smaller pieces and determine where each function falls under prohibitions, restrictions, or exceptions. Although the structure is different for each company, the two-layer structure of a layer that is prohibited to anyone and a layer that has conditions attached appears to be common in all three documents.

Areas commonly blocked by the three companies are difficult to allow even if the model provider is changed, so they can be used as the bottom line of the company's standards. Restricted categories are different from prohibited. This is an area that can be permitted if conditions such as human supervision and notification are met. Since conditions and wording vary from company to company, you must check each document in correspondence.

Enforcement progresses in stages: contact, use restrictions, suspensions, closures, and policy documents are updated as technologies and risks change. Anthropic also says it will continue to update its policy. So, if you leave a record of the decision along with the supporting document, the location of the relevant phrase, and the date of the version you read, you can check the basis again later.

In practice, we recommend the following sequence: First, break down the functions. Second, for each feature, we find and display its category in the three documents. Third, if it reaches a prohibition, it does not do it, and if it reaches a limit, conditions such as human review or notification are included in the design. Fourth, if an exception was made, write down the reason. Fifth, record the basis and edition date. These five steps may seem cumbersome, but once you make them, you can reuse them over and over again. If you follow these five steps, even if the same question comes up again, you will be able to extract evidence from the record and write it down without reading from the beginning.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Adhering to one company's policy does not mean that it is acceptable for another company's model. Additionally, not all activities are permitted just because they are not on the common prohibited list. Be sure to check the restriction categories and conditions together.

checks.intro: Check out for yourself the common no-go categories you just saw. This confirmation is not logged and you are free to retry.
checks.q: What is the most appropriate reason for using the commonly prohibited categories in the three companies' policies as the 'bottom line' of the company's standards?
options: This is because three companies have written policies with the same wording, so reading just one document is enough.
This is because it is an area where it is unlikely to be permitted even if you change companies, so it is a minimum standard.
Because activities not listed in the general prohibition are permitted in any company.
This is because the enforcement of a common ban is weaker than that of a restricted category, so it can be applied without burden.
checks.explain: A common prohibition is an area that is difficult to allow even if the model provider is changed, so it can be set as the minimum standard for the company.

wrong.0: The way it is structured and worded varies from company to company. This is why we compare the tables of contents side by side.
wrong.2: Just because something isn't in the common prohibition doesn't mean it's permissible. Each company has separate categories and conditions of restrictions.
wrong.3: The key point is not the issue of enforcement intensity, but the fact that this is an area that does not change even if you change companies.

checks.correctFeedback: That's right. The basis for the bottom line is the commonality that it is difficult to allow in any company.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Unfortunately, the reason for the bottom line lies elsewhere. Recall again the nature of the common prohibition.

checks.intro: Match the nature of prohibition and restriction, exception and enforcement. For each item on the left, choose an appropriate explanation from the right.
checks.q: Match the following policies with their characteristics:
left: Google's automated decisions for high-risk areas
Google's consideration of education, records, science, and art
Contact, use restrictions, suspension, closure of Gemini API documentation
right: Activities that have permission from the system owner are excluded from the ban
Escalating enforcement from warning to termination
Prevents decisions that greatly disadvantage individuals without human oversight
Reasons for making exceptions to the ban depending on the situation
checks.explain: Restriction categories are areas where conditions are attached, while exceptions and enforcement steps are defined separately.
checks.correctFeedback: All four pairs were matched correctly. The distinction is made that limitations, exceptions, and enforcement are different layers.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Some matches are incorrect. Re-divide which items are conditions and which are exceptions or executions.

checks.intro: Think about the order of things you look at when judging a customer-facing chatbot. Arrange the items in the appropriate order.
checks.q: Place the customer service chatbot in the right order by checking where it reaches the policy.
items: I see if they are pretending to be human or not.
checks.explain: If you break down the functions and look at them in the order of data, decisions, and congestion, the policy items you reach are revealed one by one.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. The flow starts from functions and narrows down to data, decisions, and identity.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. First, think about what needs to be broken down so you can see the rest.

glossary.def: This is a bundle of prohibitions from Anthropic policies that apply to all users and all uses.
This is an area that is explicitly blocked by the policies of all three companies. These include child exploitation, terrorism and weapons, fraud and malware.
Although it is not prohibited, it is an area subject to conditions such as human supervision and notification.
A process of automatically or manually examining input and output and retaining them for a certain period of time to look for policy violations.
Policy documents are updated as technologies and risks change. This is why the date of the version is kept in the judgment record.

misconceptions.myth: All industries not included in the policy are permitted.
misconceptions.fact: Anthropic policies are based on usage, not industry. Even in the same industry, prohibitions, restrictions, and permissions vary depending on the purpose.

misconceptions.myth: If one company's policy is followed, it will be accepted in another company's model.
misconceptions.fact: The document structure and scope of restrictions are different. You must check the items in each document by matching them.

misconceptions.myth: A restricted category is effectively a ban.
misconceptions.fact: Restricted categories are areas that may be permitted subject to conditions such as human review or notice. It should be read separately from prohibition.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: Policies are read category by category, not from scratch.
The common ban among the three companies becomes the bottom line of the company's standards.
Restricted categories come with conditions such as human review.
The decision record includes supporting documents and the date of the version.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Which features of our work most closely fall into common prohibited or restricted categories?
